chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): Beware of riding on a red saddlecloth, for it is a saddlecloth of Satan.

key_terms.إِبْلِيس: Iblis (Satan), the rebellious jinn who refused to prostrate before Adam and became the adversary of humankind
key_terms.إِيَّاكَ: Warning formula meaning 'beware' or 'avoid'; a strong cautionary address in classical Arabic
key_terms.مِيثَرَة: A padded or cushioned saddlecloth or riding cover placed on an animal for comfort and adornment

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet prohibit riding on a red saddlecloth in Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) relates a directive from the Prophet (SAWW) to Imam Ali (AS) prohibiting the use of red saddlecloths or cushioned riding covers, declaring them to be the saddlecloth of Iblis (Satan). This narration is part of a chapter on the proper equipment of riding animals and reflects early Islamic guidance on avoiding displays of ostentation and luxury in personal accessories, which were associated with arrogance and the adornment of evil. The prohibition was understood by Shia scholars as an expression of the Prophet's concern to keep Ali and the believers away from worldly extravagance linked symbolically to Satan.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan Bin Sadeyr who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said to Ali<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Beware of riding on a red saddlecloth, for it is a saddlecloth of Satan<sup>la</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from his father from Hanan ibn Sadir who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, once said to Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘You must never use a red saddlecloth; it is the saddlecloth of Satan.’”
